item.title: 🎧 LISTEN #1 — Jason & Scot Show: EP378 - The Amazon Briefing, Pt 2
item.content:encoded:
Score: 80/100 | Listen Fully | Confidence: low

Originally published 15 Sep 2026

Directly addresses core technical challenges in retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) and search/recommendation architectures. Offers a practical, pre-retrieval query clustering framework that dynamically tunes top-k retrieval, significantly cutting token cost while improving retrieval F1.

Summary

This research paper presents a pre-retrieval query clustering framework to solve the brittle nature of static top-k document retrieval in RAG systems. Standard fixed top-k approaches cause over-retrieval (wasting tokens and introducing noise) on simple queries, while under-retrieving on complex queries. The authors propose an offline method that measures per-query difficulty using NDCG and derives a saturation point (k*) from the NDCG-k curve. To avoid expensive online computation, queries are clustered in embedding space, assigning a recommended top-k retrieval depth using a mean-plus-variance rule targeting ~95% coverage. At runtime, incoming queries are mapped to clusters in constant time to pick the optimal k. In full-traffic testing, the approach improved F1 score by over 36% while reducing token usage by 14% on low-complexity clusters without sacrificing precision.

Key Ideas

  • Static top-k retrieval introduces systematic inefficiencies in RAG: simple queries over-retrieve (driving up LLM token costs and noise), while complex queries under-retrieve (causing recall failure).
  • Dynamic top-k retrieval can be executed in constant time by clustering query embeddings offline and assigning retrieval depths based on NDCG-k saturation curves and a mean-plus-variance coverage rule.
  • Deploying pre-retrieval query dynamic depth achieved a 36%+ F1 improvement while cutting token usage by 14% on low-complexity queries in production search traffic.

Implications

AI and personalization architects can implement pre-retrieval query clustering to optimize latency, API token spend, and retrieval precision across enterprise product search and conversational AI agents.
